title: Short Stuff: Petticoat Rulers
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the "Petticoat Rulers," the all-female town councils and women mayors elected in late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century western and Midwestern towns. They discuss Jackson, Wyoming, which in 1920 elected an all-female council and its first woman mayor, Grace Miller, who appointed women to top posts. They also cover Susanna Salter, the first woman elected mayor in the US (Argonia, Kansas), Mary Loman of Oscaloosa, Kansas, and Mary Woolley Chamberlain of Kaysville (transcribed as "cannab") Utah. Topics include Wyoming's early women's suffrage, the towns' reforms (back-tax collection, leash laws, littering rules, street cleanup, streetlights, a cemetery), the Pure Foods Club later known as the Birthday Club, and the long gap before women were again elected to Jackson's council in the 1980s and a woman mayor in 2001.

segments.title: Opening: Petticoat Rulers of Jackson, Wyoming
segments.summary: Josh introduces the topic of women serving in town government in the 1800s, noting Oscaloosa, Kansas and Kaysville, Utah, and then Jackson, Wyoming, which in 1920 elected an all-female council and its first woman mayor.

segments.title: First women mayors and Wyoming suffrage
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Susanna Salter as the first woman elected mayor in the US, in Argonia, Kansas, after men put her on the ballot as a prank. They note Mary Loman's election in Oscaloosa and Wyoming's early women's suffrage in 1869.

segments.title: Early reforms by the women councils
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the Kansas and Utah councils collected back taxes and how Mary Woolley Chamberlain of Kaysville, Utah enacted leash laws and a daily tax on traveling salesmen to protect local business.

segments.title: Election margins and Jackson's civic reforms
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss the two-to-one election margins, a council member beating her husband, and Jackson's reforms: criminalized littering, ended cattle grazing in the town square, graded streets, added street lamps, expanded electrical service, and started a cemetery. Historian Morgan Albertson's view that the Petticoat Rulers shaped the town is also covered.

segments.title: Grace Miller quote and the long gap in women's leadership
segments.summary: Grace Miller's quote about thrifty, home-style government is shared. The hosts note that Jackson did not elect women to its council again until the 1980s, and its next woman mayor, Jeane Jackson, was elected in 2001.

segments.title: Pure Foods Club and the Birthday Club
segments.summary: The women were originally members of the Pure Foods Club, where the idea to run for office was hatched. The group still meets twice a month today as the Birthday Club, and men are now allowed.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh salutes the Petticoat Rulers and the women who shaped the country, and the episode closes with the show credit.
